summary:
Radar for 6 Oct 2026, GLP-1 focus. The best openings are new stories that our own snapshots haven't picked up yet, where creators have done little so far:
1. **Trevogrumab + semaglutide (COURAGE, Phase 2, accepted by The Lancet).** Lean-mass loss was 4.2% vs 7.3% at 52 weeks. This fits our muscle pillar well, and the headline-decoder title formula suits it.
2. **The NYU Mendelian-randomisation study on GLP-1 and male-pattern hair loss.** It's in the Washington Post and Newsweek and is a searchable side-effect question. The honest answer is "genetic proxy, not drug users".
3. **The Wegovy/NAION vision-loss story.** A KXAN case report on 5 Oct is rising on Yahoo, so it's urgent but needs careful handling. We can pair it with the reassuring tirzepatide retinopathy data.
4. **Petrelintide and amylin.** This crossed into mainstream news (US News/HealthDay, 5 Oct), so it has moved from emerging to rising.
5. **Survodutide in NEJM (SYNCHRONIZE-2).** Our edge is an estimand decoder: 13.1% if people stayed on treatment vs 9.8% counting everyone randomised.

Lower but useful: the addiction pillar (Medscape, 6 Oct: semaglutide/tirzepatide linked to fewer overdoses in veterans, which held against insulin and SGLT2 inhibitors but not against metformin), skin conditions (hidradenitis suppurativa), the safiglipron pill (China-only Phase 3), the 'GLP-1 supplement' myth-bust, and stopping and rebound (Noom ad).

Peaking or already covered, so only worth doing with a fresh angle: the retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 Lancet paper, orforglipron ACHIEVE-4, Ozempic nails and REMODEL kidney mechanisms (C1 10-05).

Rejected: GLP-1 'microdosing'. It's trending in Yahoo Creators coverage but is banned by our guardrails.

Kids' GLP-1 prescribing is a caution item. The audience is adult parents, and the reported figures need checking against the Pediatrics paper.

candidates.topic: Trevogrumab + semaglutide (Regeneron COURAGE Phase 2, 52 weeks): lean mass fell 4.2% vs 7.3% on semaglutide alone (about 42% relative preservation); thigh MRI substudy about 70% of muscle loss prevented; total weight loss not meaningfully changed
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Can a drug protect muscle on semaglutide?' Answer: early Phase 2 says lean-mass loss was smaller. It's experimental and unapproved, and the full Lancet paper is still to come. Then pivot to what works today: enough protein (unless your clinician has told you to limit it) plus strength training. Say clearly that weight loss on semaglutide is mostly fat and not only muscle.
keywords: how to keep muscle on Wegovy
candidates.why_now: Regeneron's 52-week data came out on 1 Oct at EASD and has been accepted by The Lancet. Medical Daily covered it on 3 Oct and Inc. on 4 Oct ('could make Wegovy more effective'). Mainstream health creators haven't covered it yet, and it ties straight into our proven muscle-on-GLP-1 pillar.

evidence.signal: Lean mass −4.2% (trevogrumab 75 mg + semaglutide) vs −7.3% (semaglutide alone) at 52 weeks; ~70% thigh muscle loss prevented on MRI; accepted in The Lancet
Mainstream pickup on 3 Oct; reports that overall weight loss wasn't meaningfully increased
Primary company source for figures

candidates.topic: Do GLP-1 medicines cause male-pattern hair loss? NYU Langone Mendelian-randomisation study (J Invest Dermatol): genetically higher GLP-1 receptor activity linked to about 7% higher odds of male-pattern hair loss
candidates.angle: Search-style question: 'Does Ozempic cause hair loss in men?' Answer honestly: this is a genetic-proxy study, not a study of men taking the drug, and the 7% higher odds is a small effect. Contrast it with the more common, usually temporary shedding (telogen effluvium) after rapid weight loss. Cover what helps (enough protein, not crash-dieting) and when to see a GP or dermatologist.
candidates.why_now: The Washington Post covered it on 3 Oct after ScienceDaily, Newsweek and ABC30, so it's spreading from science news into mainstream outlets. Hair loss is one of the most-searched GLP-1 side effects. Our Ozempic hair-loss long-form predates this study, so this is a fresh hook.

evidence.signal: Primary institutional source describing the JID study and its genetic method
Mainstream pickup; experts caution that it doesn't show drug users are more likely to lose hair
Science-press coverage; 22 genetic variants used as a proxy

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and sudden vision loss (NAION): what the Austin Wegovy case means, how rare it is, and which eye symptoms need urgent care
candidates.angle: A calm explainer for a fearful headline. Explain what NAION is and its usual risk factors (diabetes, high blood pressure, sleep apnea). Say what's known: observational studies suggested a link, European regulators have listed it as a very rare possible side effect, and Novo Nordisk says no causal relationship has been confirmed. Then the practical part: sudden painless vision loss in one eye means same-day urgent care, and tell your prescriber about any eye history. No fear-mongering, no stopping advice.
candidates.why_now: The KXAN story (5 Oct) was syndicated by Yahoo the same evening, and law-firm SEO pages are already ranking for 'Wegovy blindness'. People are searching with fear, and there's little balanced, evidence-based content out there.

evidence.signal: Case report of NAION after Wegovy; ophthalmology groups say causation is not proven; Novo statement
National syndication = rising reach

candidates.topic: Petrelintide (amylin analogue): 10.7% average weight loss at 42 weeks vs 1.7% placebo, with GI side effects much closer to placebo than GLP-1s; now in mainstream news as 'a new class with fewer side effects'
candidates.angle: Decoder: 'Is petrelintide the gentler GLP-1 alternative?' Explain amylin as a partner hormone to GLP-1, give the 10.7% vs 1.7% numbers and why that's less than tirzepatide (separate trials, not head-to-head), and the tolerability trade-off. Say it's Phase 2 and not approved as of Oct 2026, and that combos (CagriSema, EloraTZP) are where amylin may matter most.
keywords: new weight loss drug fewer side effects
candidates.why_now: It moved from journal/EASD (emerging in earlier snapshots) to US News/HealthDay on 5 Oct and TIME's 'next generation' piece. That's the classic jump into mainstream news, while YouTube coverage is still thin.

evidence.signal: Mainstream: amylin drugs with lower GI side effects
Primary trial publication
Over 10% loss, fewer side effects than incretins on average

candidates.topic: Survodutide in NEJM (SYNCHRONIZE-2, 76 weeks, adults with overweight or obesity + type 2 diabetes): 13.1% if people stayed on treatment vs 3.1% placebo, but 9.8% vs 3.9% counting everyone randomised
candidates.angle: 'Survodutide: 13.1% or 9.8%?' Use it to teach the two ways trials count results, and never compare across them. Add the A1C wins (up to 29.5% reached HbA1c below 5.7% vs 4.0% on placebo) and that GI side effects were more common. Frame comparisons to tirzepatide as separate trials. Use the paper's participant count, not the press release's.
candidates.why_now: NEJM publication on 1 Oct and the review in Contemp Clin Trials keep it alive. We touched SYNCHRONIZE-2 on 10-05, so only an estimand-decoder angle adds value now.

evidence.signal: Primary publication
Up to 13.1% (efficacy estimand)
Specialist news coverage, 1 Oct

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and the eyes: linked to lower diabetic retinopathy risk in a large observational cohort (Ophthalmology), and no increased retinopathy risk in the SURPASS-CVOT retina substudy
candidates.angle: Positive counterweight to the vision-scare news: 'Does Mounjaro harm or help your eyes?' Randomised-trial substudy data show no increase. Observational data show a lower risk, which is 'linked to', not proven protection. Remind people with diabetes about yearly eye screening.
candidates.why_now: Medical Economics flagged on 3 Oct that tirzepatide is tied to lower diabetic eye disease risk, during the same week as the Wegovy vision-loss story. Eye safety search demand is spiking.

evidence.signal: Population cohort: lower incident and progressive DR vs lifestyle intervention
SURPASS-CVOT retina substudy: no increased retinopathy risk
Institutional release; observational association caveat

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and tirzepatide linked to fewer overdoses in veterans with type 2 diabetes and opioid use disorder (VA target trial emulation): lower risk vs insulin and SGLT2 inhibitors, but not vs metformin, sulfonylureas or DPP-4 inhibitors
candidates.angle: Benefits-beyond-weight, early research: 'Could semaglutide help with addiction?' Report exactly who was compared and the null comparisons, and say it's observational and that RCTs are underway. Never suggest it as an addiction treatment. Add support-line info with real hours.
candidates.why_now: Medscape ran 'GLP-1RAs Show Promise in Opioid Overdose in Veterans' on 6 Oct, and the Wake Forest 'neuroscience of motivation' piece came out on 5 Oct. The addiction angle is resurfacing and creator coverage is sparse.

evidence.source: J Clin Psychiatry (VA target trial emulation)
evidence.signal: Lower all-cause overdose vs insulin and SGLT2i; not vs metformin, SU, DPP4i
Stable primary citation
39% lower repeat overdose risk (observational)

candidates.topic: 'GLP-1 supplements' vs the real medicine: Lemme rebrands its GLP-1 supplement after legal scrutiny, as 'natural GLP-1' products multiply
candidates.angle: An attributed correction/myth-bust: 'Does a GLP-1 supplement work like semaglutide?' No. Explain how your own GLP-1 hormone lasts minutes while semaglutide is engineered to last about a week. Cover what actually nudges your own GLP-1 modestly (protein, fibre, eating order) without claiming it replaces the medicine. Name no products as recommendations.
candidates.why_now: Nutraceutical Business Review covered the Lemme rebrand under legal scrutiny on 6 Oct, along with the Phaseolean 'GLP-1, PYY' marketing push. People already believe the 'natural GLP-1' claim, which is ideal myth-bust territory.

evidence.signal: Lemme rebrands GLP-1 supplement after legal scrutiny

candidates.topic: What happens after stopping semaglutide or tirzepatide? Noom's ad stokes rebound fears (Adweek, 6 Oct). What the trial extensions actually show about regain and the health markers that drift back
candidates.angle: Evergreen refresh with a news hook: 'Do you regain weight after stopping Ozempic?' Use the trial-extension figures exactly (STEP 1 extension; SURMOUNT-4 withdrawal). Explain that obesity is a chronic condition, any decision to stop belongs with your prescriber, and the habits that help (protein, strength training). Compassionate, no shame.
keywords: what happens when you stop Mounjaro
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen, spikes 2–5 days around the ad
candidates.why_now: The Noom ad controversy (Adweek, 6 Oct) and Yahoo Creators' 'what happens when you stop Ozempic' (6 Oct) are re-raising the question. It ties to our SURMOUNT-1 3-year snapshot and the WashU stopping/heart-risk story.

evidence.signal: Noom ad stokes GLP-1 rebound fears
Weight nadirs and regain in adults with obesity/overweight and prediabetes on tirzepatide

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and hidradenitis suppurativa: JAMA Dermatology cohort links use to lower all-cause mortality and fewer cardiovascular events, plus a new nationwide JEADV cohort (3 Oct) and a Clin Dermatol review on psoriasis
candidates.angle: Benefits beyond weight, skin edition: 'Can semaglutide help painful skin conditions like HS and psoriasis?' All observational, and the people taking GLP-1s may differ in other ways. Say who was studied and that it's not an approved use. Encourage people to talk to their dermatologist.
candidates.why_now: Three dermatology publications in a week (JEADV nationwide cohort 3 Oct, Clin Dermatol psoriasis review 1 Oct) suggest a building research wave, and there's almost no consumer video coverage.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 use linked to lower mortality and CV events in HS
New cohort study in HS
GLP-1 RAs in psoriasis management

candidates.topic: GLP-1 prescriptions for children aged 8–11 with obesity rose sharply 2019–2026 (Pediatrics, >3.5 million children; 94% of those prescribed had severe obesity; no approval under age 12)
candidates.angle: For parents in our audience: 'Are kids under 12 getting Wegovy?' Give the verified numbers from the Pediatrics paper (some news figures look inconsistent, so check them), say what's approved (age 12+) and what isn't, cover nutrition-deficiency concerns, and the questions to ask a paediatrician. No shame and no weight talk aimed at children.
candidates.why_now: Pediatrics published this week, with local TV pickup on 5 Oct (News4JAX, WKBN), STAT's reassuring op-ed, and Yahoo Health on nutritional deficiencies.

evidence.signal: Primary trend paper 2019–2026
Use remains rare but is rising rapidly
Local mainstream pickup, 5 Oct

candidates.topic: Safiglipron, a GLP-1 pill taken without fasting rules: Phase 3 OUTSTAND-2 vs dapagliflozin in China. HbA1c 0.22–0.40 points lower than dapagliflozin at 32 weeks, weight −2.35% to −4.17% vs −3.60%
candidates.angle: New-pills pillar: 'Safiglipron: a GLP-1 pill with no empty-stomach rule?' Compare the oral options (Wegovy pill approved Dec 2025, orforglipron/Foundayo, safiglipron). Say it was Chinese sites only, has an active comparator, and is not approved in the US/UK. Weight loss was modest and similar to dapagliflozin.
candidates.why_now: A second Nature Medicine paper landed on 5 Oct, following the 29 Sep placebo-controlled RCT. Pill-search demand is high ('Ozempic pill', 'semaglutide tablet' queries), and almost nobody has covered safiglipron.

evidence.signal: Phase 3 vs dapagliflozin; non-inferior all doses, superior at 90 mg
Early T2D placebo-controlled trial

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 in The Lancet: 20.8% vs 4.0% placebo at 80 weeks (12 mg, adults with obesity + T2D). Differentiated angle: 'Is retatrutide approved yet?' as of Oct 2026, and why online 'retatrutide' isn't the trial drug
candidates.angle: Huge search demand ('is retatrutide approved', 'retatrutide weight loss drug'). Answer the approval-status question with a date hedge, give the verified Lancet numbers with estimand, cover side effects from the paper, and repeat the Lilly-attributed warning about research-peptide versions. Never point to any source.
candidates.why_now: Search-query feeds show dozens of retatrutide queries plus 'FDA concerns unapproved GLP-1 retatrutide'. We've already done TRIUMPH-2, so only the approval-status/FAQ angle is fresh.

evidence.signal: Peer-reviewed Phase 3

candidates.topic: 'Ozempic nails': nail detachment reported by 39.3% of GLP-1 users vs 8.7% of controls in a self-reported EADV survey; newser now covering
candidates.angle: A searchable side effect with honesty: self-reported survey, possible recall bias, nail changes often follow rapid weight loss or illness. Cover what helps and when to see a doctor.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 3 snapshots and now in general news (newser, 5 Oct), but momentum is flattening (66→70→64).

evidence.signal: General-news pickup 5 Oct

candidates.angle: Not for production. Our guardrails ban microdosing and self-titration content, and the coverage invites dosing questions and gray-market sourcing. If we touch it at all, only a general line elsewhere saying dosing decisions belong to your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Trending creator coverage, but outside brand guardrails.

evidence.signal: 'Microdosing GLP-1s like Ozempic is everywhere'
